project_type: Python multi-service RAG system: Telegram bot (telegram_bot/), ingestion CLI (src/ingestion/), apartment catalog scripts (scripts/apartments/), Qdrant vector store. Issue ***REMOVED***1401 is in domain:retrieval (apartment search filtering).
build_system: uv (pyproject.toml + uv.lock); Make targets wrap uv run; Docker compose for full stack but not needed for this repo-only verification
test_framework: pytest with pytest-xdist (parallel), pytest-timeout=30s default; markers include 'not legacy_api and not requires_extras and not slow' for the fast lane; live-service tests live under tests/smoke/, tests/integration/, tests/e2e/ and are out of scope for this repo-only issue
test_command: PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-n auto --dist=worksteal' make test-unit  (fast unit lane); for focused changed-files: uv run --python 3.12 pytest tests/unit/services/test_filter_extractor.py tests/unit/services/test_query_filter_signal.py tests/unit/scripts/ -q --timeout=30
verification_instructions: 1) `make lint` (ruff check src/) and `uv run ruff check telegram_bot/ tests/ scripts/` for touched paths. 2) `uv run mypy src/ telegram_bot/ --ignore-missing-imports --no-error-summary` (or `make type-check`). 3) Focused pytest run for the modified test files plus the new regression tests. 4) Full unit lane: `PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-n auto --dist=worksteal' make test-unit`. 5) Per AGENTS.md and verify:repo-only label: do NOT run docker compose, do NOT touch live Qdrant; the schema decision is verified by mocking qdrant_client.QdrantClient in unit tests.
setup_instructions: uv is pre-installed in the sandbox per the steering docs. Run `uv sync --all-extras --all-groups` (or `make install-all`) once at task start. Subsequent test runs use `uv run --python 3.12 pytest ...`. No services need to be running for this issue (verify:repo-only label).
environment_constraints: verify:repo-only — must not require live Qdrant, Redis, Postgres, or Telegram. All Qdrant interactions must be mocked. Network availability has not been confirmed by tooling; assume COMMON_DEPENDENCIES (uv index reachable) is the worst case. If `uv sync` fails due to network, the coder should report it as blocked rather than guess.
contribution_requirements: Per AGENTS.md and .kiro/steering/agent-workflow.md: (a) test-first for behavior changes (this is a behavior change to filter schema); (b) include fresh verification evidence (paste pytest summaries) and explicitly list skipped checks; (c) keep service boundaries (`telegram_bot/services/` for business logic); (d) preserve observability patterns; (e) keep AGENTS.md / docs/QDRANT_STACK.md in sync with the code change.
key_patterns: Two distinct Qdrant collections coexist with different payload conventions: (1) document/CSV pipeline collection `gdrive_documents_bge[_scalar|_binary]` uses payload nested under `metadata.*` (writers add the prefix in src/ingestion/indexer.py and runtime filter builders prepend `metadata.` in telegram_bot/services/qdrant.py._build_filter); (2) standalone `apartments` collection uses top-level fields (no prefix), with its own _build_apartment_filter in telegram_bot/services/apartments_service.py. Tests for setup scripts use `unittest.mock.patch('scripts.<mod>.QdrantClient')` to inspect create_payload_index calls — see tests/unit/scripts/test_apartments_setup_collection.py for the exact pattern.
directory_structure: telegram_bot/ — Telegram bot with services/ (filter extraction, qdrant facade, apartments service, query analyzer), dialogs/ (funnel, filter_dialog), agents/ (apartment_tools), setup_qdrant_indexes.py (entry-point that creates indexes for the document/CSV collection — name targets config.qdrant_collection which defaults to gdrive_documents_bge). src/ingestion/ — unified+legacy ingestion pipelines; indexer.py creates the document/CSV collection schema and writes data nested under `metadata.*`; chunker.py parses CSV "Мебель" column to bool key `furnished`. scripts/ — operational scripts; setup_binary_collection.py creates the *_binary variant with metadata.furnished BOOL; scripts/apartments/setup_collection.py creates the standalone `apartments` collection with top-level is_furnished BOOL. tests/unit/ — fast tests; services/ for service-level units; scripts/ for AST/mocked setup-script regression guards. docs/QDRANT_STACK.md — canonical doc that already documents the divergence in an 'Important discrepancies' bullet; that bullet is the deliverable to replace.
design_decision: Two canonical fields, one per collection: (A) Document/CSV collection (gdrive_documents_bge*): canonical `metadata.furnished` BOOL — matches what src/ingestion/chunker.py already writes and what src/ingestion/indexer.py + scripts/setup_binary_collection.py already index. The legacy `metadata.furniture` KEYWORD index in telegram_bot/setup_qdrant_indexes.py is broken (data type mismatch with what the chunker writes) and must be retired. (B) Standalone apartments collection: canonical top-level `is_furnished` BOOL — already consistent end-to-end (parser, ApartmentRecord, payload, index, filter builder, dialog, tool). No change needed in lane B. Runtime filter producers that target the document/CSV collection (FilterExtractor._extract_furniture, QueryAnalyzer SYSTEM_PROMPT, query_filter_signal reason label) must emit `furnished: bool` so qdrant._build_filter produces a BOOL match against `metadata.furnished`. Migration safety: setup_qdrant_indexes.py is idempotent and logs 'already exists' for pre-existing indexes; the legacy `metadata.furniture` keyword index, if present in a deployed collection, has zero data hits and may be left in place or removed by an operator via Qdrant API. Documented migration note in docs/QDRANT_STACK.md.
